subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should OpenClaw add manifest-declared install-time config intent for third-party plugins, and what allowed paths, confirmation, conflict/array behavior, provenance, and uninstall guidance are required?
rationale: This changes plugin install from enabling package metadata to letting third-party metadata request persisted user config changes, which crosses product, upgrade-safety, and security boundaries that automation cannot choose alone.

options.title: Define guarded config intent
options.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates against current config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and classifies or limits sensitive paths before writing.

options.title: Keep manual setup for now
options.body: Reject manifest-driven writes and keep plugins using docs, setup flows, provider auth, or explicit openclaw config patch commands until a safer contract is designed.

options.title: Gate through package trust
options.body: Require ClawHub/package trust metadata or a plugin setup flow to carry any install-time config request before core accepts it.

recommendation.title: Define guarded config intent
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates against current config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and classifies or limits sensitive paths before writing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the clearest product/security routing comment and has recent manifest/install documentation history.
